correctness.rationale: Every k>=1 follows from greedy-arch necessity/sufficiency and exhaustive partition by first two Lyndon letters. Length 2k+1 start 01 implies no 00, exactly k zeros and one doubled 1-run, which must be the final run by rotation comparison. Start 00 forces 001 plus k-1 length-two arches; any 10 arch yields an explicitly lexicographically smaller rotation from the final 10-to-01 boundary. Each surviving witness has k arches and is lex minimal under rotations. Length-2k k>=2 Lyndon impossibility and k=1 exception are covered. The unrestricted count is unique-arch arithmetic. Direct pattern membership and greedy-arch implementations agree exhaustively through k=6; full word enumeration checks the theorem through k=9; larger witnesses are checked through k=200. Finite tests do not prove infinity; the written combinatorial proof does.

value.rationale: The exact first-slack intersection is an all-order structural classification, not a single finite enumeration: among (k+2)2^k almost-shortest binary k-universal words precisely two are primitive lex-minimal representatives of their own rotations. The one-symbol necessity for Lyndon k-universal hosts at k>=2 and the explicit two-word rigidity resolve a natural near-optimal constrained supersequence question. The proof exhibits a nontrivial interaction between greedy arch locations and cyclic lex order, not a mere relabeling or specialization of a previously counted table.
